meta-description: 💼 Amazon SDE2 Interview – Round 2 Experience

My Round 2 at Amazon shifted from pure DSA to problem-solving + system thinking, with a strong focus on how you reason.

🧠 Coding / Design Problem

The core problem was based on an N-ary Tree:

➡️ Given a list of nodes in an N-ary tree and a level L, return all nodes present at that level.

That part was straightforward using level-order traversal.
🔗 https://lnkd.in/ghgfxPPz

🔍 Follow-up (Where it got interesting)

Now assume:
	•	Nodes can be added or removed dynamically
	•	You must return the count of nodes at any level in O(1) time

This pushed the discussion towards:
	•	Pre-computing & maintaining level-wise counts
	•	Updating counts efficiently on insert/delete
	•	Trading a bit of space for constant-time queries
A great test of data structure design under changing constraints, not just coding.
🔗 https://lnkd.in/g--NmUZc

⭐ Leadership Principles Covered

The interviewer clearly evaluated solutions through Amazon’s LP lens:

1️⃣ Learn & Be Curious
	•	Exploring multiple approaches
	•	Asking clarifying questions
	•	Willingness to optimize beyond the obvious solution

2️⃣ Deliver Results
	•	Driving the solution to completion
	•	Handling edge cases
	•	Making sure the final approach actually meets the stated time complexity

🎯 Takeaway

Amazon interviews are less about knowing a trick and more about:
	•	How deeply you understand fundamentals
	•	How you adapt when constraints change
	•	How well you balance correctness, performance, and clarity

Solid round. Great learning experience.

If you’re preparing for Amazon or similar product companies — think beyond the first solution. The follow-ups matter.
